key_insight: The paper introduces an automated running error analysis framework that computes forward rounding-error estimates alongside finite element kernel values to reveal and diagnose numerical instability as the code runs.
engineering_relevance: This gives FEM developers a practical way to debug ill-conditioned formulations, assess mixed-precision safety, and improve robustness in performance-critical simulation kernels.
method: Use Running Error Analysis (REA) to propagate an error estimate concurrently with each computed value.
Implement REA in FFCx via a C++ backend with templated kernels over a custom arithmetic type carrying value and error.
Apply the framework to detect cancellation in Neo-Hooke assembly and to study error behavior on a near-degenerate mesh.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two demonstration cases and states that the REA implementation typically adds only about 2–4x performance overhead.
watch_item: The approach introduces extra runtime cost and is tied to kernel generation support, so integration overhead and performance impact should be considered for large-scale production workflows.
paper_title: Running error bounds in finite element kernels
